level_basis: Production exact-count/list/class APIs with typed total/row/cell admission, checked exponents, disjoint borrowed DP updates and bounded explicit traversal lifecycle; no level follows from a mathematical title.

formal_specification.domain: Counts n<=1000; positive nonincreasing partition lists additionally admitted by caller row count and conservative count*n cell cap; arbitrary-order positive cycle lists admitted by checked total and factorial bound 20000, including empty lists.
behavior: Accept n<=1000 including the boundary; reject larger arguments before DP vector allocation with exact typed operation/argument/maximum fields.

After admission initialize the empty partition count to one. For each allowed part ascending, update totals ascending by adding the already-updated same-part predecessor. Disjoint slices borrow the summand without an owned BigUint clone. Return exact p(n), including p(0)=1.

Compute the admitted exact count first, reject count above caller row budget, then reject conservative count*n above 1048576 cells. Equality is allowed. Only then construct all positive nonincreasing rows summing to n, in descending lexicographic order. Zero has exactly the empty row. This bound can conservatively refuse a request whose actual shorter rows would fit.

Private admitted n only. Explicit frames record remaining sum and next descending part; current is the path prefix. Zero remaining emits an owned row, exhausted frames backtrack, and each positive choice decreases both the parent cursor and child remaining. Preserve original recursive traversal order with a constant machine call stack and at most n+1 frames.

Reject any zero cycle length first, then checked total-sum overflow. Admit factorial(total)<=the supported argument domain before map/power work. Count exact multiplicities, checked-convert each exponent, and compute n! divided by product length^multiplicity * multiplicity!. Empty and unsorted cycle lists are supported; all accepted positive lists give an integral class size. Oversized totals now refuse before multiplicity work, intentionally changing diagnostic argument priority for some formerly oversized inputs.

invariant_argument: Admission fixes n<=1000 before n+1 or DP allocation; all totals are in part..=n with part>=1. Thus total-part<total<n+1. split_at_mut(total) creates disjoint before/current slices, current[0] and before[total-part] are valid, and BigUint += borrows a distinct value. No floating point, fixed-width count accumulation, truncation or saturation occurs.

After completing part k, ways[t] counts multisets of positive parts<=k summing to t. Initially only t=0 has one empty multiset. Multisets using no k are counted by the previous ways[t]; removing one k from those using k gives exactly ways[t-k] already updated for the current k because totals ascend. These disjoint classes prove the recurrence. At k=n every positive partition of n is covered. BigUint carries exact nonnegative counts. The independent generalized-pentagonal recurrence checks every n from 0 through 1000.

The output guard first requires p(n)<=limit, then p(n)*n<=1048576 in exact BigUint arithmetic. Every output row has at most n scalar entries. Consequently the eager retained scalar cells are bounded by this product, with a separate empty-row case at n=0. This is a conservative upper bound, not the exact sum of row lengths. Workspaces for counting are explicitly allowed before the output guards; no allocation-free refusal promise is made.

While the frame stack is nonempty, the current positive nonincreasing path has length frames.len()-1, and the top remaining plus its prefix sum equals n. Each frame cursor is at most its remaining and the preceding chosen part. A positive cursor selects a valid part and decreases before descending; the child remaining is strictly smaller. Zero remaining emits exactly the path; a zero cursor after all children backtracks without emission. Parent cursor preservation simulates the previous recursive call order. Paths and choices are unique, all legal choices occur, and output order is descending lexicographic. The finite depth is at most n+1; the explicit stack makes machine call depth constant.

Conjugacy admission scans for zero before summing, preserving that first error even if another field could overflow. checked_add refuses sum overflow. factorial(n) then admits n<=20000 before any multiplicity map or powers. Positivity implies list length and each multiplicity are at most n, so checked multiplicity increments and u32 exponent conversion are safe. Their typed fallback branches remain defensive and unreachable on admitted input. This new total-first lifecycle intentionally changes some oversized-input diagnostic details; accepted values remain unchanged.

Each positive cycle multiset of total n determines a symmetric-group conjugacy type: remove 1-cycles to obtain Mathlib cycleType with all members>=2 and sum<=n; the removed count is n minus that sum. Mathlib proves actual realization, conjugacy size and denominator divisibility. Grouping the nontrivial multiset product gives product length^multiplicity, while 1-cycles contribute 1^count=1 and their count! fixed-point factor. Thus the source denominator is positive, divides n!, and BigUint integer division loses no fraction. Input order is irrelevant because exact multiplicities are stored in a BTreeMap.

All five production bodies meet maxima CCN 9, cognitive 7, nesting 3. Counting performs O(n squared) exact BigUint additions in O(n) values. Counting values are bounded by the positive-composition count 2^(n-1) for n>0, so their bit growth is finite under n<=1000. Enumeration visits at most the output-path prefixes and copies each required owned row, with O(p(n)*n) scalar work/storage upper bound under the conservative cap. Conjugacy scans caller input, then has map size, factorial and exponent work bounded by admitted total 20000. Standard-library and BigUint implementation costs/allocator availability remain TCB; no global heap or constant-time promise.

Public inputs are borrowed or scalar and no caller data is mutated. Local workspaces drop on typed failure. Output vectors and BigUint values are owned results; raw returned values are not authority or intrinsic proof certificates.
